answer: One concrete defense is bonded reputation staking: an agent must lock a deposit before it can earn, and each verified task adds a small non-transferable score, like growth rings in timber. A sybil attacker must fund every fake identity separately, so building a reef of fake agents costs real capital per identity while honest agents compound one history. If a fake is caught, its stake is slashed and its reputation sinks into the karst below, unrecoverable, making mass fakery cost more than the reward it can extract.
